newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks weak in morning, investors cautious.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks weak in morning, investors cautious.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks were easier in Monday morning trade with light selling on banking stocks after the Dow Industrials fell nearly 140 points on Friday on fears U.S. interest rates may rise this week, brokers said.
The Hang Seng Index eased 73 points, or 0.52 percent, to 13,988 in early trade. Turnover was HK$2.46 billion.
"The market is falling in tandem with Wall Street last Friday," said Gary Wong, sales director at Vickers Ballas.
"People are a little bit cautious but I think properties should hold up quite well."
Edwin Cheung, dealing director at Taiwan Securities, said a substantial correction was unlikely and the main index should find good support at the 13,800 mark.
Brokers said trading would likely be range-bound ahead of Tuesday's meeting of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee, which sets U.S. interest rate levels. -- Hong Kong Newsnews (852) 2843 6369
